analysis.investment_thesis: CIE Automotive India trades at INR 490 — a 58% premium to its Graham Number of ~INR 311 (√22.5 × EPS₂₅ ₹21.8 × BVPS ₹196.5), offering no margin of safety whatsoever. With P/E at 22.5x and P/B at 2.49x, Mr. Market is pricing in growth this auto-parts supplier has yet to demonstrate consistently.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage: D/E of 0.06 with borrowings collapsed from ₹1,648 Cr (2020) to ₹426 Cr (2025) — exactly the balance sheet fortitude Graham demands
Strong and consistent free cash flow: FCF positive every year 2020–2025, reaching ₹885 Cr in FY25, well in excess of financing obligations
Interest coverage of ~50x (EBIT ₹1,362 Cr / Finance Cost ₹27 Cr) — de facto zero financial stress
key_risks: P/E of 22.5x far exceeds Graham's ceiling of 15x; P/B of 2.49x is 66% above his 1.5x limit — the investor is paying for future hopes, not proven asset value
Revenue growth of only 6.5% CAGR over 9 years is barely ahead of inflation; operating margin of 8.19% is thin and cyclically exposed to OEM pricing pressure
Net loss in FY2022 (₹-136 Cr) breaks the consecutive positive-earnings requirement; 'Other Income' of ₹-749 Cr that year signals opacity in the income statement
red_flags: Reported at a 58% premium to the Graham Number — no margin of safety
FY2022 net loss breaks the 5-year consecutive earnings test; the ₹749 Cr 'Other Income' write-down in that year was never clearly explained in public disclosures
Subsidiary of a Spanish parent (Participaciones Internacionales Autometal) — related-party transfer pricing risk and dividends may be repatriated ahead of minority shareholders
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CIE Automotive India is a fundamentally sound auto-parts manufacturer with genuinely excellent debt discipline, but it fails every one of my quantitative valuation filters. At INR 490, the P/E is 22.5x against my hard ceiling of 15x, and P/B is 2.49x against my 1.5x limit. The Graham Number, computed as √(22.5 × ₹21.8 EPS × ₹196.5 BVPS), yields roughly ₹311 — implying the stock must fall 37% simply to reach fair value by my method, let alone offer the margin of safety I require. Revenue has grown only 6.5% CAGR over nine years and operating margins remain a slim 8.19%, both telling me this is an ordinary cyclical supplier, not a franchise business.

The business does earn points for financial stewardship: debt has been systematically retired (₹1,648 Cr → ₹426 Cr in five years), FCF is robust and consistent, and interest coverage is a staggering 50x. ROE of 11.8% and ROCE of 14.7% are adequate but unexceptional. The FY2022 net loss and the unexplained ₹749 Cr negative "Other Income" entry remind me that earnings quality here requires scrutiny. I would watch this stock patiently for a price closer to INR 300–310 before considering a position — at that level the margin of safety would become meaningful. At today's price, the intelligent investor simply waits.
